one_sentence_failure_summary: After the FastText pip install failed due to a missing C++17 compiler and git was absent, the agent substituted scikit-learn (Logistic Regression / Naive Bayes) models instead of installing build tools to compile FastText, producing a joblib file renamed to model.bin that is incompatible with fasttext.load_model and also failed to meet the 0.62 accuracy threshold.
t_err_evidence: At step 10, after git was not found (step 9), the agent ran 'pip install scikit-learn' and explicitly planned to use TF-IDF + Logistic Regression instead of seeking an alternative way to install FastText (e.g., apt-get install build-essential). This is the decisive wrong action that locked in a spec-violating approach.
t_commit_evidence: By installing scikit-learn at step 10 and immediately drafting the TF-IDF pipeline, the agent committed fully to the scikit-learn path; it never attempted to fix the C++ compiler environment thereafter, making the fastText-incompatible outcome inevitable given its subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: At step 22, the first model run printed 'Test accuracy: 0.5485', which is below the required 0.62 threshold — the first explicit observable signal that both the model format and accuracy requirements are unmet.
trigger_explanation: The real environment obstacle was a missing C++17-capable compiler (revealed at step 8) and absent git (step 9), both needed to build FastText. Rather than fixing the environment (e.g., apt-get install build-essential git), the agent treated the obstacle as a dead end and substituted an entirely different, spec-incompatible library (scikit-learn) at step 10.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8 shows the pip fasttext wheel build failing with 'RuntimeError: Unsupported compiler -- at least C++17 support is needed!'. Step 9 shows 'bash: git: command not found'. Both are clear disconfirming signals before the agent's commitment at step 10.
